subject: Materials Science
title: Passivation: Self-Healing Armor
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Passivation: Self-Healing Armor.

hook.text: Stainless steel doesn't stain — not because it can't corrode but because it heals itself instantly.

buildup.text: Chromium in stainless steel reacts with oxygen to form a thin, invisible oxide layer — just nanometers thick.

discovery.text: This passive film blocks further corrosion — scratch it and it regrows in milliseconds.

twist.text: Chloride ions penetrate the passive layer — that's why stainless steel corrodes in seawater and road salt.

climax.text: Aluminum, titanium, and chromium all self-passivate — their thin oxide films protect billions of products.

punchline.text: The best corrosion protection is a film so thin you can't even see it.

quiz.question: How does passivation protect stainless steel?
options: A thick paint layer covers the surface
A thin chromium oxide film forms and self-heals when scratched
The steel is coated in plastic
